summary: Iter 44 (description translation quality fix + AI cost logging/report/budget feature) tested end-to-end. Backend pytest suite: 23/26 passing (3 flakes are Gemini free-tier 429 rate limits when hammering ro/pl fresh translations in a burst — environmental, not code). Description SSE stream produces fluent, Hangul-free output in bg/en/ro/pl for 4 different Korean listings; cached listing is served from db.translations in ~0.2s and NO new db.ai_calls row is written; ai_calls rows have full schema (ts/day/provider/model/kind='description'/lang/in_tokens>0/out_tokens>0/cost_usd>0/ok/ms) and failed rows carry an error string. Admin surface: GET /api/admin/ai-usage returns full shape for days=7|30|90 with billing.available=false (no ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY in preview), 401s without token and with a bad token; PUT /api/admin/ai-budget persists, clamps to 0.5..1000, returned value shows up in the next /ai-usage; POST /api/admin/ai-report/send returns 200, stores db.ai_reports and the entry is listed under reports[]. Admin UI in /bg/admin?tab=ai renders every required data-testid, chart draws, range buttons switch, budget save shows the Bulgarian toast, report send refreshes the reports list, no console errors, all copy Bulgarian. Regression: POST /api/search still works, returns *_t translated fields, and db.ai_calls contains the description kind at minimum. Car detail translate button on 42379471 streams Korean→English fluently (1600 chars, no Hangul).

minor.issue: Under Gemini free-tier rate pressure (both providers unavailable), the SSE emits a single 'translation is unavailable right now' error frame. Expected in preview because ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is invalid AND Gemini free-tier RPM is low, but any concurrent user hitting the page during a Gemini 429 window sees the same error — no in-server retry after backoff. Consider a 15–30s retry on Gemini 429 inside _desc_gemini (the reply carries retryDelay), or fall through to EMERGENT_LLM_KEY (which is chained in for label translations but NOT in the description path).

integration_issues.issue: After a page reload the description panel intentionally re-mounts with the Korean original and the translated text does NOT auto-render — the visitor has to click 'Преведи текста' again. The second click IS instant (~0.2s from backend cache), so technically 'cached forever'. But the review wording 'stays after a page reload (cache)' is a UX expectation the current code deliberately does not honour (see DescriptionPanelBody.js comment: 'never on page load'). If the intent is that a returning visitor sees the translation without re-clicking, either persist the last choice in localStorage per-carId+lang, or auto-fetch when a description translation exists in the cache. Not a bug per the code's own contract — flagged for clarity.

action_items: OPTIONAL: In translate._desc_gemini, honour a Gemini 429 by waiting the RetryInfo delay ONCE before returning empty, so a single free-tier hiccup does not make the SSE panel say 'unavailable' when a retry 25s later would have succeeded. Same pattern _gemini_call already implements for the labels path.

OPTIONAL: In translate._desc_llm's Gemini fallback path, when both anthropic and gemini fail, try EMERGENT_LLM_KEY via _emergent_call (it is chained in _providers for other kinds but not reached from _desc_llm). Would remove the last single-point-of-failure for descriptions.

UX DECISION (not a bug): DescriptionPanelBody deliberately shows Korean on every remount. If review wording 'stays after a page reload' is a requirement, wire a small localStorage flag or eager-fetch the cached translation when the panel mounts.
critical_code_review_comments: aicost.billed(): the ai_billing cache never reads today's row when admin_key is missing — that's fine, but the `known >= days - 1` short-circuit means if the admin key is later added the historical days will NOT be back-filled unless the caller passes refresh=True on a fresh day. Consider a one-shot background back-fill when admin_key first appears.

translate.meter() uses asyncio.get_running_loop() + create_task inside a fire-and-forget; the RuntimeError catch swallows metering when called from a sync context (which is fine for tests) but there is no fallback write — a batch translation invoked from an on_startup sync hook would silently lose its usage rows. Very edge-case.

translate._desc_llm: `on_chunk` is invoked for each streamed piece BEFORE the final message is validated with _looks_translated. If the model streams partial text and then produces something that fails the check, the browser has already been shown the (potentially bad) chunks and the endpoint returns done=true anyway. Consider validating the accumulated output before emitting the final 'done' frame, and yielding a fail sentinel instead.

aicost.check_budget picks the alerted flag out of ai_reports but overwrites the doc with $set — the merge could clobber an earlier `emailed:true` field on the same day. Use $set on individual keys or read the existing doc first.

server.translate_description_stream builds a queue with an asyncio.Task but does not cancel the task if the client disconnects; a slow LLM run keeps running and metering after the browser is gone. Wrapping the generator in try/finally that cancels `task` would tidy this.

success_rate.backend: 88% (23/26 passing — 3 failures are Gemini free-tier 429 on parallel ro/pl fresh streams; not a code issue)
success_rate.frontend: 100% — every requested data-testid on /bg/admin?tab=ai is present, all interactions (range switch, budget save, report send, reload) work, Bulgarian copy correct, no console errors, car detail translate streams Korean→English fluently
